title: If I Could Change One Thing at WKU…
writingModel: If I Could Change One Thing at WKU — by Amir Bekzhanov

If I could change one thing about WKU, I would introduce a formal mentorship programme for first-year students. At the moment, new students are largely left to find their way by themselves — a process that is often difficult, sometimes discouraging, and occasionally completely unnecessary. If every first-year student were paired with a second or third-year mentor, the adjustment would be much smoother.

The idea is simple. At the start of each academic year, the university would match first-year students with more experienced peers from the same faculty. These pairs would meet at least twice a month. The mentor would answer questions, share study strategies, warn about common mistakes, and provide the kind of practical information that official documentation never quite captures.

If this programme existed, it would have several significant benefits. First, first-year students would feel less isolated. Many of them — I know because I was one of them — spend the first month feeling overwhelmed and unsure who to ask for help. A mentor would change that immediately. Second, the mentors themselves would benefit. Teaching and guiding someone else is one of the best ways to consolidate your own knowledge.

There is also a social dimension. If students from different years had regular, structured contact, the university community would feel more connected. Currently, year groups largely move in separate circles. A mentorship programme would break those silos down. It would create relationships that last beyond university — and in a small city like Uralsk, those relationships matter.

I acknowledge that implementing such a programme would require time and coordination. The university would need to recruit volunteer mentors, train them briefly, and establish a light administrative structure. But I don't think these challenges are insurmountable. If WKU invested in a pilot programme with one faculty first, it would be possible to measure the impact before scaling up.

If I could change one thing, it would be this. Not the curriculum, not the buildings, not the canteen food — though all of those could also be improved. The one thing that would make the biggest difference is helping students feel that they are not navigating university alone. If they felt supported from day one, everything else would be easier.
